rationale: The required preamble is import subprocess for f's subprocess.run; repr is a builtin and needs no import. f visibly contains subprocess.run, but its only reference is inside C.__repr__, and C defines only that one specifically relevant method; it has no constructor, so no spawn is routed through construction. The transcript's sole executable statement beyond the definitions is repr(C), and its argument is C itself, the class object, not an instance. By Python's special-method lookup, repr(obj) implicitly invokes __repr__ through the type of obj; the type of C is its default metaclass type, so repr(C) resolves to type.__repr__ and returns the class's canonical representation such as "<class '__main__.C'>". The instance-level __repr__ defined in C's body is stored for instances of C and is never consulted, and C is never instantiated in this transcript. Therefore f's deferred body is never entered, subprocess.run is unreachable, and the transcript executes no process-spawning path, so no finding of any class is expected. Shape boundary: this negative holds only for the class-argument form repr(C); repr(C()) would dispatch to C.__repr__, call f, and legitimately yield a finding, so that form is deliberately not used. This expectation is derived from Python data-model and call semantics, independent of any tool outcome, and the fixture is inert: executed or only scanned, nothing in it spawns a process.
